testnet._note: LEGACY stack, not source-equivalent to current code (built before owner-key notes, the canonical public-input check, batch transcript challenges and revoke_previous_vk). Redeployed 2026-08-14 to close 7 findings from an external technical review (three Critical in contracts/swap, one High in contracts/governance, plus three lower-severity fixes) — see docs/POC_IMPLEMENTATION.md's 'Update: external audit' and 'Update: live redeployment with the fast-timelock testnet build'. The `governance` binary for this deployment was built with the testnet-fast-timelock feature (VK_TIMELOCK_LEDGERS=60, ~5 minutes, vs the real 7-day production value) — see contracts/governance/Cargo.toml's doc comment on that feature; never build a production artifact with it enabled. Prior addresses (verifier CCRLI4EAT62..., governance CDCSHTT3R75M..., compliance CA2EU46YYEBJ..., token CDE7U6HTLMDF..., swap CDPPRPAVKUJG...) predate all seven fixes and are superseded.

testnet_tranche2._note: Tranche 2 live validation stack: token::transfer/transfer4's relayer-fee routing, token::unshield's change-note output (new 7-input Unshield circuit), and swap::commit_swap's min_amount_out early bound check are all built from this source. The verifier is administered directly by the deployer (no governance timelock), same as the Tranche 1 stack. Verifying keys registered for Shield, Transfer(2x2), Unshield, Transfer4x4 and SwapFairness. The deployer is also an approved relayer on both token and swap (their own, separate ApprovedRelayer allowlists). Live-validated transactions (see docs/TESTNET_DEPLOYMENT.md's Tranche 2 section): a relayer-submitted, fee-paying transfer(); a re-measured transfer4(); a partial unshield() that produced a real change note; a full commit_swap -> execute_swap -> reveal_and_claim lifecycle exercising min_amount_out; and a live cancel_swap() recovery.

testnet_final._note: Fresh stack deployed 2026-10-13 (scripts/testnet_deploy_stack.sh), carrying the reviewer-remarked fixes on top of everything the 2026-10-08 stack already had: circuits/swap/swap_fairness.circom's min_amount_out is now a direct, asset_out-denominated value the swap creator supplies (not derived from amount_in by a flat slippage percentage, which was asset-blind and unsound for a non-1:1 pair - see docs/TRANCHE2_DELIVERABLES.md section 3); contracts/token now refuses any positive relayer fee for an asset with a nonzero custody_shortfall (FeeRefusedDuringShortfall); the SDK now ships TESTNET_INDEXER_URL, covered by a drift test against this record. verifier, governance, token, swap and compliance are all freshly deployed and wired (governance's own admin-of-verifier relationship meant a fresh governance -- needed to point at the fresh token -- could not retain admin rights over the old verifier, which has no admin-transfer mechanism, so verifier had to be fresh too). viewing_keys is reused unchanged from the prior stack (no coupling to the others, no live state to lose, no initialize()/admin at all). Governance is the verifier's and token's admin; swap and compliance admin is the deployer zkella-testnet-deployer; guardian is zkella-testnet-guardian. Governance was built with the testnet-fast-timelock feature, so timelock_ledgers() is 60 (about 5 minutes), NOT the 7-day production timelock. Verifying keys for all six circuits (including the fixed SwapFairness) are live via the timelock from genesis this time, not rotated in after the fact. Native XLM is approved on the token through governance. Compliance sanctions root is the empty-list root (sentinels only), not a real sanctions list.
